note: THE DOCUMENT REGISTRY. Greg, S112: 'we need to put the list of our working docs in the store or a section of the sop so one doesn't get forgotten about.' Same disease as A-17 one level up - a document that is on no list goes stale silently, and nothing can report it. MEASURED THE DAY THIS WAS BUILT: 55 of 151 tracked research/kalshi/*.py files were absent from KALSHI_TRADING.md, the index whose stated job is 'every Kalshi file, what it does, current vs old'; and PLANT_MAP.md had been EDITED THAT SAME SESSION while naming none of the four plant components built in it. So mtime is not staleness - CONTENT is, and only a content gate catches this.

classes.LIVE: must be kept current. A gate exists where the content can be computed; otherwise the trigger is stated and the andon can only remind.
classes.RENDER: GENERATED from a store. Never hand-edit - edit the store and re-render. Gated byte-identical by store.py check.
classes.VAULT: frozen, sha256-manifested. A change is a versioned vault event on Greg's go, never an edit. Gated by verify_gold.py.
classes.RECORD: dated and finished. NEVER updated - a handoff, kickoff, drop-in, ledger or findings memo describes the session that wrote it. Editing one is falsifying the record.
classes.ARCHIVE: moved out of the live surface deliberately. Consulted, not maintained.

close_out_trio.note: Greg, S112: 'update all of our docs other than the 3 ending ones.' These three are written LAST, at close-out, because they summarise everything else. They are excluded from mid-session doc sweeps by design.

documents.role: the master pointer - one-line state, the read-first order, standing rules. Deliberately lean: it points at detail, it does not hold it.
documents.update_when: close-out only (member of the close-out trio), plus any STANDING rule change (D34 landed here mid-session because it is standing)

documents.role: THE FILE INDEX - every Kalshi file, what it does, current vs superseded. Curated prose per session, plus a GENERATED completeness appendix.
documents.update_when: any new research/kalshi file, same session it is created
documents.gate_note: every tracked research/kalshi/*.py must be NAMED somewhere in the file. The curated sections carry the judgment (current vs old); the generated appendix carries the completeness, so nothing can be silently missing.

documents.role: the append-only binding-decision ledger, D1..D35 plus nonconformances, with the instance-inline rule.
documents.update_when: a decision is made - add to store/decisions.json, then render

documents.role: THE SPEC BOOK, binding. Every station of the group cycle with verbatim spawn templates. Its appendix is a RENDER; the body is change-controlled prose.
documents.update_when: any change to how a run is spawned or scored - versioned diff on Greg's go, never an edit in place
documents.gate_note: the appendix is gated byte-identical against store/sop_templates.json; the prose body is change-controlled, not generated

documents.role: what runs where: every standing process, its host, branch, trigger and heartbeat. If a process is not on this map it is not a standing process.
documents.update_when: any new standing process, host, or plant control tool
documents.gate_note: every .py the SOP names must appear here - non-circular, because the list is derived from another document rather than hand-kept

documents.role: THE TRACKED WORK REGISTRY (D30). plant_status reads it at bring-up so an open item can be counted, not remembered.
documents.update_when: IN THE SESSION a thing is agreed - A-17's lesson: a commitment living in another item's prose is invisible to the count

documents.role: THE BRAIN - plays, mechanisms, doctrine, instances. Schema brain-schema-1.
documents.update_when: a merge, a retirement, or a doctrine finding. Never hand-edit structure - brain_schema.py validates and migrates

documents.role: key inventory - names and holders ONLY, never values.
documents.update_when: a key is added, moved or retired. NOT rotated during the walk (standing)

documents.role: what the business is and what winning looks like.
documents.update_when: a scope or target change - D32 and D35 are both mission-level

documents.role: short-horizon task list. SUBORDINATE to OPEN_ITEMS.json - if the two disagree, the registry wins.
documents.update_when: opportunistically; the registry is the system of record

documents.role: the agent handbook - roles, the five-specialist era, who owns which day class.
documents.update_when: a role is added or changed (state_auditor was the last)

documents.role: the small-model conformance sweep, report-only.
documents.update_when: a new nonconformance class is found

documents.role: how the brain is structured and how to read it.
documents.update_when: a schema change

documents.role: canonical specialist rule file - blind and refine read the SAME committed file byte-identically (D-S105). A separate copy could drift.
documents.update_when: versioned vault event on Greg's go only

documents.role: the FROZEN gold vault, chmod 0444 + sha256 manifest, three off-site copies.
documents.update_when: never in place

documents.role: the full detail of one session. The system of record for what happened.
documents.update_when: written once, at close-out. NEVER edited afterwards

documents.role: the next session's opening instruction set. Its work list is GENERATED from the registry (A-9) so a DONE item cannot appear as a live instruction.
documents.update_when: written once, at close-out

documents.role: pre-DROP_IN era session openers.
documents.update_when: never - superseded by DROP_IN

documents.role: per-session findings memos, ledgers, briefings and merge proposals. Dated by construction.
documents.update_when: never. A later correction goes in a LATER document or in the brain, never by rewriting the record

documents.role: the full OD/crypto-era and physics-era research, verbatim. Moved out of always-loaded context because it is history.
documents.update_when: never
